content:
The first Home Ownership Scheme (HOS) flat built using the "Modular Integrated Construction" (MiC) method, On Pak Court in Kwun Tong, has only been occupied for 15 months. Recently, owners have reported that the building's exterior wall paint is peeling, blistering, flaking off, and growing moss. FactWire visited the site on Thursday (the 8th) and observed workers on suspended platforms repainting multiple areas, with no more blistering visible on the exterior walls. However, the adjacent On Wa Court, also built using MiC, has large areas of blistering on its exterior walls, similar to On Pak Court, and multiple cracks have appeared on the estate's boundary walls, with efflorescence seeping out. Some residents are worried that problems will persist after the Housing Department's maintenance period expires, and owners will have to pool funds for repairs. They complained about "spending millions on a defective building" and hope the Housing Department will permanently maintain the estate's common areas.

On Pak Court and the adjacent On Wa Court are the Housing Department's first HOS developments using the MiC construction method, where residential units are prefabricated in mainland factory facilities, with the structure, plumbing, electrical work, and interior decoration all completed, before being transported to Hong Kong and assembled into buildings.

Blistering on On Wa Court's exterior walls

FactWire arrived at Anderson Road this afternoon and saw that repair work on On Pak Court's exterior walls was largely complete, while water seepage marks and cracks remained on the estate's boundary walls. However, On Wa Court, which also uses MiC and is just a street away, has the same issues with its exterior walls. One entire facade of the 28-storey building shows blistering across all floors, with obvious unevenness at the joints between levels. The estate's boundary walls have multiple thin diagonal cracks, with efflorescence seeping out and leaving white crystals on the surface. Mr and Mrs Cheung, On Wa Court residents who moved in just two months ago, said there are no leaks inside their unit, but they have noticed the orange-painted sections of the exterior wall have loose, peeling paint.

Recently, some On Pak Court owners told the media that the residents' group chat contained numerous complaints about ongoing leaks since occupation. Some found water leaks in the kitchen and bathroom when collecting their keys, large areas of blistering and paint flaking on building walls, exterior wall pipes leaking and growing moss, and cracks on the exterior walls of high floors, with the sealant joints of the modular units shrinking and splitting open.

Toilet pipe leak discovered

Ms Wong, an On Pak Court resident who collected her keys about half a year ago, told FactWire that a leaking toilet pipe was discovered at the time and was repaired by the contractor, with no subsequent leak issues inside the unit. However, she is unhappy that a new building is already peeling paint after just one year of occupation and is worried about problems arising after the maintenance period. "What if owners are required to pool money for major repairs?" Ms Wong hopes the Housing Department will "guarantee quality to the end" and permanently handle maintenance of common areas. She added that workers on suspended platforms have been doing repairs at the estate recently, with paint splattering onto her laundry, forcing her to dry clothes indoors. She bluntly stated: "Spending millions on a defective building."

Cracks appeared on canopy soon after

Another owner, Ms Tsang, moved in earlier this year, and cracks appeared on the canopy soon after. The contractor carried out repairs, though it is unknown whether cracks will reappear during future windy and rainy weather. She noted that fortunately, the owners are united and have contacted the District Council and the media to follow up, which has forced the Housing Department to carry out repairs. She is not worried about having to bear high maintenance costs in the future.

On Wa Court was built by Shui On Construction and completed in August last year, with occupation beginning in November. The two blocks of On Wa Court provide 990 units, ranging from 296 to 495 square feet, with an average price of HK$7,030 per square foot and unit prices ranging from HK$1.81 million to HK$3.77 million. On Pak Court is a simultaneous project by the same contractor, with foundation work beginning in February 2022 and completion three years later. The single block has 420 units with usable areas ranging from 291 to 498 square feet, averaging HK$7,000 per square foot, priced from HK$1.77 million to HK$3.73 million, with phased occupation beginning last July.

The Housing Department earlier told the media that after receiving complaints about On Pak Court in late July this year, it immediately urged the contractor to carry out comprehensive repairs. After drone inspections, it was estimated that dust had not been thoroughly cleaned before painting at some exterior wall locations, or the primer was not applied evenly, which was attributed to poor paintwork craftsmanship.

In addition, the department found no cracks in the walls and believes these were actually water stains on the exterior wall after rain. As for reports of "MiC module sealant joints shrinking and splitting," the Housing Department confirmed after on-site verification and review of records that this was not the situation described by owners, but rather a workmanship defect where wall paint overflowed onto the sealant during application. Cleaning and repairs at those locations have been completed, and there is no leakage in any unit.
